Excellent packing by Belgium in 1961 at Nantes prevented England from gaining a 4th consecutive victory, but we had the consolation of seeing that fine cross-country runner Basil Heatley, gain his first International title.

Laurie O'Hara on the last leg (5¼ miles) had the unenviable task of chasing Basil Heatley. At one time we thought he was going to catch up and we could look forward to a sprint finish, but the experience of Heatley prevailed and Coventry stayed in front to win by 25 seconds.
1960 - John Merriman leads Gerry and Gordon Pirie in the National C.C.Champ. at West Bromwich. Basil Heatley was the winner and Gerry finished 4th.
Basil Heatley, although "retired" from representative running, is still a very consistent performer and provides the Godiva team with the stability it sometimes needs.
Coventry were deserved winners on the day and proved that 6 in 60 is now necessary to win the 'National'----the 'retired' Basil Heatley closing-in in 63rd place.
His effort of 28:10 was only 5 seconds away from being 3rd fastest, behind Freary and Tipton's Jim Wright, and was just one second better than Basil Heatley, out again up front for Coventry.
